aim: The grip force and friction calculator: part weight in four units, a material pair carrying its own friction coefficient, an acceleration profile, orientation, contact count and safety factor, resolved into a per-finger and total required grip force, a seven-line formula breakdown and a conditional warning box.
contract: - Root `div.tool-container`, form `#gripForm`, submit `#calcBtn`. The tool ships its JS INLINE
in the component template (`length(js_content) = 0`), so there is no `/tools/assets/*.js`
sidecar to blank -- the driven checks are mutated at the inline script or at the element it
writes into.
- **The arithmetic is the contract.** F_tan = m*g + m*a; F_grip = F_tan / mu; total = F_grip * SF;
per finger = total / n. Display bands: below 1 N in mN to 1 dp, at or above 1000 N in kN to 2 dp,
otherwise N to 1 dp. Two `computed_values` vectors pin both a plain case and the unit-conversion,
kN-band and all-four-warnings case:
* defaults + 2.5 kg + 5 m/s^2  -> 46.3 N per finger, 92.6 N total, 37.0 N load, mu 0.80, 2 contacts;
* 10 lb, PTFE (mu 0.10), 20 m/s^2, 4 fingers, SF 1.5 -> 507.1 N per finger, 2.03 kN total, 135.2 N load.
Both vectors were DERIVED from the page's own inline JS and then matched the live tool exactly,
so the golden is corroborated two ways rather than blind-captured.
- **The reveal is a SEPARATE claim from the arithmetic, and it has to be.** `computed_values` reads
the text of a `display:none` subtree perfectly well -- measured here twice, once by removing the
reveal and once by an isolating probe that hid the panel from CSS alone with no JS change. In both
cases every computed value still matched. So `submitting-reveals-the-results` carries the
visibility claim on its own; without it a tool that computes correctly and shows the visitor
nothing would pass this fence.
- The warning box is asserted in BOTH directions -- absent on the safe vector, present on the risky
one -- because a warning that never fires and a warning that always fires are both defects and a
one-sided check cannot tell them apart.
- Check order is load-bearing: the evaluator drives ONE page per profile in declaration order, so the
default-vector checks precede the second vector, and every state-dependent assertion sits
immediately after the gesture that produces it.
- **`no_auto_fix` is set.** The page is `rebuild_policy='owned'` on another lane's site; a failing
verdict must escalate to human review rather than point `tool-improver` at protected markup that it
could only turn green by weakening the assertion.
proof_note: single canonical component, no forks; page resolves under the Tier-4 lookup as tool-grip-force-friction-calculator; served 200 with DOCTYPE at 38,873 bytes
mutants: 13/13 caught, 13/13 checks OBSERVED red, baseline green
accommodations: none -- no same-origin fetches, baseline green on the local copy unmodified

aim: MatchMatrix: a gripper selection matrix. One application spec (mass, part size, surface material, contact count, acceleration, safety factor, IP requirement) is turned into THREE requirement figures -- friction-grip force, direct holding force and a dynamics-adjusted equivalent payload -- and every gripper in a 10-strong index is assessed against whichever figure its manufacturer actually publishes, then ranked.
contract: - Root `div.tool-container`, form `#mmForm`, run button `#mmForm .btn-run`, reset `#mmReset`.
JS is INLINE in the template (`length(js_content) = 0`); there is no script sidecar to blank.
- **The three requirement figures are the arithmetic contract.** dyn = m*a*S; friction-grip
F = dyn/(mu*n); direct hold F = dyn; equivalent payload m' = dyn/g. Pinned at 1 dp, 1 dp and
2 dp respectively, at two vectors.
- **The RANKING is a second, independent claim, and it is the one a spec edit moves.** Cards sort
by verdict rank then by headroom, so the fence pins the leader by name and verdict, plus a
mid-table entry on the first vector. Two mutants demonstrate the halves come apart: cutting one
published jaw force drops that gripper out of the FIRST vector's ordering only; cutting the
strongest force changes the SECOND vector's leader only.
- **Both branches of the summary line are exercised.** Vector A (2.5 kg, 40 mm, steel, 2 jaws,
defaults) yields `4 of 10 indexed grippers meet the requirement.` with Schmalz SGM-HP 50
leading and Robotiq 2F-85 third; vector B (8 kg, 80 mm, glass, 3 jaws, IP67) yields the
zero-match branch, `No gripper in this index meets the requirement...`, led by Zimmer. A fence
that only ever saw the non-empty branch could not tell a broken filter from a demanding spec.
- **`computed_values` compares RENDERED text.** The verdict badge carries
`text-transform: uppercase`, so the golden is `MATCH` / `NO MATCH`, not the `Match` / `No match`
the JS builds. A golden copied from the source string is wrong for any transformed element --
this cost one red trial here and is the right way round, because it pins what the visitor sees.
- **The reveal and the reset are separate claims from the arithmetic.** `computed_values` reads a
`display:none` subtree perfectly well (measured on the sibling grip-force tool, twice), so
`running-reveals-the-results` carries the visibility claim and `reset-clears-the-results` the
teardown. The reset check is deliberately LAST of the driven checks: it wipes the results the
earlier checks assert against, and the evaluator drives one shared page in declaration order.
- **`no_auto_fix` is set.** The page is `rebuild_policy='owned'` on another lane's site, and every
red here is a claim about published manufacturer specifications -- an automated rewriter could
only turn it green by editing the index or weakening the assertion.
